title: The Excellence of a Ruler
note: This means the ruler’s good qualities and good deeds. The word இறை is used because he protects the world in the form of the gods who guard it.

couplets.plain: An army, people, food, ministers, friends and forts: whoever has all six is a bull among rulers.
couplets.pm: A ruler with all six limbs, the army, the land and its people, wealth, ministers, allies and forts, is like a bull among rulers. Without even one of them, rule doesn’t work, which is why Sanskrit writers call them limbs. Having them all is the cause of his victory.

links.reason: Measures rulers against each other and says who stands as the bull among them.
The army stands first in the list of six.
Food, the crop that is the realm’s wealth, comes third.
Friends, the Tamil’s நட்பு, come fifth.
Forts close the list of what such a ruler must hold.

couplets.plain: Fearlessness, giving, understanding and drive: a ruler’s nature is never to lack these four.
couplets.pm: It is a ruler’s nature to have these four without a break: firmness, giving, understanding and drive. Drive is the mind rising to action. Understanding serves all six limbs, giving serves the army and the others serve action. Qualities recede as others show, but if these recede a ruler loses much, so they must always show.

links.quote: a ruler’s nature is never to lack these four

links.reason: Leads the four things a ruler may never lack.
A ruler’s giving is second among the four that must not fail.
Understanding, the Tamil’s அறிவு, is the good sense a ruler needs third.
Drive closes the list of what no ruler can go without.

couplets.plain: Wakefulness, learning and resolve: these three never leave those who rule the land.
couplets.pm: For one with the fortune to rule the land, these three never leave: speed in the matters at hand, the learning to understand them, and manliness. Manliness means doing a thing quickly, looking at nothing else, so it is called resolve here. Learning serves all six limbs, and the others serve action.
couplets.note: தூங்காமை is literally not sleeping. He reads it as not delaying.

links.reason: Speaks of those who rule the land, not of people in general.
Wakefulness, the Tamil’s not sleeping, opens the three.
Resolve completes the three: the firmness to settle a matter and hold to it.

couplets.plain: A ruler keeps to righteousness, removes what is wrong, and has an honour that never slips from valour.
couplets.pm: A ruler keeps without fail to the righteousness laid down for him: studying, sacrificing and giving, and also bearing arms, protecting life and crushing enemies. He stops unrighteousness such as killing and theft in his land. His honour never falls short of valour: he won’t strike the young, the old or those who flee.

links.quote: keeps to righteousness, removes what is wrong
links.reason: Requires of him first that righteousness never fail and that wrong be removed.

links.quote: an honour that never slips from valour
links.reason: Charges him with an honour that never slips.

couplets.plain: A ruler is one who can create, gather and guard, and share out what is guarded.
couplets.pm: He alone is a ruler who can open new ways for wealth to come, gather what comes, guard it from enemies, thieves, kin and officials, and spend it on righteousness, wealth and pleasure. Giving to gods, sages, the poor and renown serves righteousness. Elephants, army and forts serve wealth. Halls, pools and groves serve pleasure.
couplets.note: The Tamil doesn’t say what is created and gathered. He supplies wealth.

links.quote: A ruler is one who can
links.reason: Holds the ruler himself to these four tasks.

links.quote: create, gather and guard, and share out what is guarded
links.reason: Describes the office as four tasks: to create, gather, guard and share out.

couplets.plain: If a ruler is easy to see and not harsh in speech, his land will be praised above all others.
couplets.pm: If a ruler is easy to see for those who seek justice and those who beg for help, and speaks harshly to no one, the world will rank his land above all lands, and so him too. Being easy to see means sitting in the great hall with sages and the worthy, in a good mood. They will call his land better than heaven, free of hunger, disease and enemies.
couplets.note: He supplies “the world” as the one who praises. The Tamil can also mean that the land praises its ruler.

links.quote: his land will be praised above all others
links.reason: Ties the land’s standing to two habits of its ruler.
Asks that a ruler be easy for people to see.

links.quote: easy to see and not harsh in speech

couplets.plain: Whoever can give and protect with sweet words will find the world is just as their own word would have it.
couplets.pm: For a ruler who can give with sweet words and protect, this world joins with his renown and is all he intends: it yields everything he wishes. Giving means giving people what they need, and protecting means keeping them from harm by his retinue and his enemies. These are hard, so it says “can”. He will rule the whole earth.
couplets.note: சொல் can mean his word or, as he takes it, his renown.

links.quote: the world is just as their own word would have it
links.reason: Promises one who gives and protects with sweet words a world that follows their word.

links.quote: give and protect with sweet words
links.reason: Praises giving when it is done with sweet words.
The gift is to come with sweet words, the Tamil’s இன்சொல்.

couplets.plain: A ruler who does justice and protects will be held the lord of his people.
couplets.pm: A ruler who does justice himself and protects the people from others is a man by birth, yet by his deeds he is set apart from men and raised up as their god. Justice is the way the books on righteousness and statecraft lay down.
couplets.note: இறை can mean lord or god. The plain reading says lord. He says god, set apart from men by his deeds.

links.reason: Raises the ruler who does justice and protects to the rank of lord of the people.

couplets.plain: The world rests under the umbrella of a ruler with the character to bear words bitter to his ears.
couplets.pm: The world rests in the shade of the umbrella of a ruler who can bear the words of those who rebuke him, though his ears can’t stand them, looking to what comes of them. Good character here means fine discernment. Since he doesn’t fail in righteousness and statecraft, he will rule the whole earth himself.

links.quote: The world rests under the umbrella
bear words bitter to his ears

couplets.plain: Giving, kindness, a straight sceptre and care for the people: a ruler with these four is a light among rulers.
couplets.pm: A ruler with these four is a lamp to all rulers: giving people what they need, showing everyone warmth with a bright face and sweet words, doing justice, and caring for people who have fallen on hard times. From such people he takes his sixth share only once their poverty has ended, and gives it up if he must.

links.reason: Giving leads the list of what makes a light among rulers.
The straight sceptre, the Tamil’s செங்கோல், is third of the four.
